title_en: Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Strengthening and Improving Administrative Adjudication Work
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Strengthening and Improving Administrative Adjudication Work

Fa Fa [2007] No. 19

High People's Courts of various provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Strengthening and Improving Administrative Adjudication Work are hereby issued to you for implementation in conjunction with the actual work of administrative adjudication.

April 24, 2007

Supreme People's Court

Opinions on Strengthening and Improving Administrative Adjudication Work

In order to earnestly implement the spirit of the Sixth Plenary Session of the Sixteenth Central Committee of the Communist Party of China, implement the Opinions of the General Office of the CPC Central Committee and the General Office of the State Council on Preventing and Resolving Administrative Disputes and Improving the Mechanism for Resolving Administrative Disputes and the spirit of the Fifth National Conference on Administrative Adjudication Work, adapt to the needs of China's social development in the new era, strengthen and improve administrative adjudication work, fully leverage the functional role of administrative adjudication, and provide stronger judicial guarantees for building a socialist harmonious society, the following opinions are hereby proposed.

I. Importance and Urgency of Comprehensively Strengthening Administrative Adjudication Work

1. Achieving the goals and tasks of building a socialist harmonious society requires administrative adjudication work to provide stronger judicial guarantees. Fully leveraging the functional role of administrative adjudication is of extremely important significance for properly handling contradictions among the people, maintaining the order of administrative management and social harmony and stability. Especially under the new situation where the number of administrative disputes is increasing day by day and collective administrative disputes are relatively prominent, the task of administrative adjudication in resolving administrative disputes, protecting citizens' rights and interests, maintaining social stability, and promoting social harmony has become more arduous.

2. The growing judicial needs of the people require administrative adjudication to pay more attention to fairness and efficiency. The increasing trend of administrative disputes not only reflects the increasingly diversified and complex pattern of social interests, but also reflects the continuous improvement of the people's awareness of rights protection according to law and the growing expectation of judicial relief. With the development of the situation and the acceleration of the pace of rule-of-law construction, the situation of the people resolving administrative disputes through litigation channels will become more and more frequent, and the requirements for the people's courts to provide effective judicial relief according to law will also become higher and higher. The people's courts must adhere to the guiding principle of "impartial justice, wholehearted service to the people," properly resolve administrative disputes through adjudicating administrative cases according to law, protect civil rights with timely relief, reduce the burden on the people with high-quality services, relieve the people's worries with speedy trials, protect the people's interests with fair judgments, and realize the people's wishes with effective enforcement, effectively solve the problem of "difficulty in filing lawsuits" in administrative litigation, and provide the people with fair and timely judicial protection.

3. Strengthening the Party's governance capacity requires further improvement of administrative adjudication capacity. The Decision of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China on Strengthening the Party's Governance Capacity takes scientific governance, democratic governance, and governance according to law as one of the overall goals of strengthening the Party's governance capacity. The Party's way of governance according to law is mainly realized through legislation, administration, and judicial activities. Attaching importance to strengthening administrative adjudication work is an inevitable requirement for improving the Party's governance capacity and an important guarantee for improving the Party's governance capacity. People's courts at all levels and all administrative adjudication personnel must continuously enhance their administrative adjudication capacity from the strategic height of strengthening the Party's governance capacity to meet the urgent need of resolving administrative disputes and internal contradictions among the people in the new era.

4. Promoting the construction of a law-based government requires further playing the positive role of administrative adjudication in supervising, maintaining, and promoting law-based administration. Governing the country according to law and building a socialist country under the rule of law is not only the basic strategy of the Party leading the people in governing the country, but also an important constitutional principle. Law-based administration is the core content of governing the country according to law; to achieve governing the country according to law, law-based administration must first be realized. In the process of building a law-based government, realizing the transformation of government functions and innovation in management methods, the people's courts, by adjudicating administrative cases according to law, supervise and promote administrative organs to comply with legal procedures, correct ultra vires and abuse of power, play an active and irreplaceable important role in implementing the requirement of law-based administration that "where there is power, there must be responsibility; power must be subject to supervision; and infringement must be compensated." At the same time, the people's courts uphold lawful and appropriate administrative acts according to law, confirming the validity of administrative acts through judicial procedures, which is also a judicial guarantee for the effective exercise of various economic and social management functions of administrative organs.

5. Joining the World Trade Organization requires the people's courts to assume new responsibilities of judicial review. The WTO agreements set clear requirements on the judicial review systems of member states. China's Protocol on Accession to the WTO also makes clear commitments by taking judicial review as an important measure to ensure the implementation of the trade system, and in accordance with the requirements of WTO rules, has amended and formulated a large number of laws and regulations. The Supreme People's Court has also formulated and issued corresponding judicial interpretations, establishing and improving the corresponding judicial review system. In recent years, administrative cases involving the implementation of WTO rules have begun to appear, especially a substantial increase in foreign-related intellectual property administrative cases. The new situation and new tasks not only expand the field of administrative adjudication, but also put forward higher requirements on the judicial concepts and judicial level of China's administrative adjudication.

6. In accordance with the requirements of the new situation and new tasks, there are still some incompatible problems and weak links in the current administrative adjudication work: First, some court leaders have insufficient understanding of the importance of administrative adjudication work and have not placed it on the work agenda as it should be, resulting in imperfect administrative adjudication institutions in a few courts, insufficient trial forces, unstable teams, and generally low quality of trial personnel; Second, some believe that administrative adjudication is difficult and risky, fearing to offend the government or relevant administrative organs, dare not exercise judicial supervision power, or knowingly render judgments against conscience when administrative acts are illegal, shifting conflicts upward. Some courts are also keen on handling non-litigation administrative enforcement cases, unwilling to accept and hear administrative litigation cases; Third, the quality of some administrative cases is not high, and individual cases are delayed for a long time without conclusion, affecting the realization of the legitimate rights and interests of the parties; Fourth, illegal interference in administrative adjudication still exists to varying degrees in some places, and "local policies" restricting the litigation rights of the parties have not been completely eliminated; Fifth, investigation and research on new situations and new problems emerging in the field of administrative adjudication are insufficient, etc. These problems affect the implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law, damage judicial authority and the image of justice, and restrict the performance of the functions of administrative adjudication. They must be taken seriously and effectively resolved.

II. Basic Experience and Main Tasks of Administrative Adjudication Work

7. Over the years, people's courts at all levels have summarized and accumulated many valuable experiences in administrative adjudication, mainly: protecting the legitimate rights and interests of administrative counterparts according to law is the primary task of administrative adjudication; correctly handling the relationship between supervision and maintenance is an important principle for fully exerting the functions of administrative adjudication; adhering to the combination of fairness and efficiency is an important guarantee for the healthy development of administrative adjudication work; adhering to the unity of legal effects and social effects is the basic requirement for carrying out administrative adjudication work; continuously improving and optimizing the judicial environment is a necessary condition for the healthy development of administrative adjudication; actively exploring new methods for properly handling administrative disputes is an important guarantee for continuously achieving new results and new development in administrative adjudication work; adhering to the leadership of the Party and consciously accepting supervision from the People's Congress and all sectors of society is the fundamental guarantee for doing a good job in administrative adjudication work.

8. For the current period and for some time to come, the main tasks of the people's courts' administrative adjudication work are: guided by Deng Xiaoping Theory and the important thought of "Three Represents," fully implement the Scientific Outlook on Development, closely focus on the guiding principle of "impartial justice, wholehearted service to the people," firmly establish the socialist judicial concept, strive to build a fair, efficient and authoritative administrative adjudication system, in accordance with the requirements of "protecting legitimate rights and interests, promoting law-based administration, optimizing the judicial environment, and resolving administrative disputes," fully leverage the functional role of administrative adjudication, and provide powerful judicial guarantees for building a socialist harmonious society.

III. Earnestly Protect the Legitimate Rights and Interests of Citizens and Promote Law-Based Administration

9. People's courts at all levels must always adhere to the theme of "fairness and efficiency," adhere to the successful experiences and effective practices in trial practice, and effectively ensure and continuously improve the quality and efficiency of administrative adjudication. They must fully understand and correctly implement the provisions of the Administrative Procedure Law and relevant judicial interpretations, strengthen the protection of the counterpart's right to sue, accept administrative cases involving citizens' personal rights and property rights according to law, and accept administrative cases involving other economic and social rights closely related to personal rights and property rights according to law. They must effectively solve the problem of administrative cases that should be accepted but are not accepted, or are not accepted in a timely manner according to law, resulting in the administrative counterpart's "difficulty in filing lawsuits"; effectively solve the problem of illegally accommodating, handling cases against the law, and harming the interests of the parties when illegal administrative acts should be annulled; effectively solve the problem of low trial efficiency in some cases, excessively long trial cycles, and delays without conclusion. Higher courts should strengthen supervision over the trial of administrative cases by lower courts, resolutely correct acts of failing to perform administrative adjudication duties and handling cases against the law according to law, and report and seriously deal with typical cases that cause adverse effects.

10. While protecting the legitimate rights and interests of administrative counterparts according to law and supervising administrative organs' law-based administration, people's courts at all levels should provide timely and strong support for administrative management activities and lawful administrative acts implemented by administrative organs according to law. They should correctly accept and promptly enforce non-litigation administrative enforcement cases according to law, supporting administrative organs' law-based administration. They should actively provide effective judicial guarantees for the functions of economic regulation, market supervision, public services, and social management implemented by administrative organs at all levels according to law. They must resolutely support, according to law, special law enforcement activities by governments at all levels and relevant administrative departments in cracking down on and sanctioning illegal acts such as land violations, violations in the financial and securities fields, intellectual property infringements, acts endangering food and drug safety, acts damaging natural resources and environmental protection, and acts harming the legitimate rights and interests of farmers, maintaining the normal order of administrative management, economic order, and social order, and maintaining the authority and good image of governments at all levels and administrative departments.

IV. Strive to Create a Good Judicial Environment

11. Among the factors currently affecting the development of administrative adjudication work, the judicial environment is still a relatively prominent issue. People's courts at all levels must firmly rely on the leadership, supervision, and support of the Party committee and the People's Congress, effectively solve problems of substituting words for law, suppressing law with power, and illegally interfering with administrative adjudication, and overcome local and departmental protectionism in administrative adjudication. For acts that interfere with, hinder, or obstruct the people's courts from accepting, trying, and enforcing administrative cases, they should promptly report to disciplinary inspection and supervision organs at all levels to obtain support.

12. We should actively promote the reform and improvement of the jurisdiction system for administrative cases, by increasing the intensity of designated jurisdiction and trial in different places, preventing and eliminating illegal local interference, and providing institutional guarantees for the people's courts to independently and fairly adjudicate administrative cases according to law.

13. Exploring the reform of the jurisdiction system should correctly handle the following issues: First, the goal must be to ensure judicial fairness. Whether it is designated jurisdiction or elevated jurisdiction, the purpose is to prevent and eliminate improper interference and ensure that the people's courts handle administrative cases fairly according to law. For cases where jurisdiction by the local basic-level court may affect fair trial, the intermediate people's court may, upon application by the parties, decide on designated jurisdiction or elevated jurisdiction to ensure the fairness of the trial. Second, combine the choice of the parties with the decision of the court. The parties may file a lawsuit with the basic-level people's court where the defendant is located, or apply to the intermediate people's court for jurisdiction, or request the intermediate people's court to designate another basic-level people's court within its jurisdiction to hear the case; whether to grant such application is decided by the intermediate people's court. Third, balance convenience for litigation and case balance. Designated jurisdiction should consider the difficulties and burdens of the parties, and follow the principle of proximity as much as possible. At the same time, the number of administrative cases undertaken by each basic-level court can be balanced through designated jurisdiction. Fourth, cooperate between the case filing division and the trial division. When deciding on designated jurisdiction or elevated jurisdiction, the case filing division and the administrative division should strengthen communication and cooperation; the administrative division may provide opinions on which court should be designated to have jurisdiction. Fifth, focus on solving the problem of fair justice in basic-level courts, and resolve administrative disputes at the basic level as much as possible. The jurisdiction of cases in intermediate people's courts and above shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of current laws and judicial interpretations.

V. Actively Explore New Mechanisms for Handling Administrative Cases

14. Administrative disputes belong to contradictions among the people, and the causes and formation of administrative disputes are often complex, and the circumstances of each administrative case are also different. Therefore, the resolution of administrative disputes must adopt multiple methods and means. In the process of trying administrative cases, the people's courts should actively explore new mechanisms for handling administrative cases in accordance with the requirements of "adhere to legality review, promote law enforcement improvement, standardize voluntary withdrawal according to law, and strive to conclude cases and settle matters."

15. On the premise of clarifying facts, distinguishing right from wrong, and not harming national interests, public interests, or the legitimate rights and interests of others, the people's courts may suggest that the administrative organ improve or change its administrative act and compensate the administrative counterpart for losses; the people's court may rule to allow the administrative counterpart to voluntarily withdraw the lawsuit. Especially for collective administrative disputes arising from social hot issues such as rural land expropriation, urban house demolition, enterprise restructuring, labor and social security, and resources and environmental protection, more attention should be paid to using conciliation methods to handle them to the maximum extent. Not only must there be skilled judicial review capacity, but also superb communication and coordination skills and mass work capacity; not only must the immediate interests of the people be protected according to law, but also be good at guiding the parties to exercise their rights legitimately and legally; not only must the fairness of individual case handling be ensured, but also the maximization of social benefits; not only must we do our own work wholeheartedly, but also be good at obtaining and relying on the support of the Party committee and the government. We must prevent and avoid intensification and transformation of conflicts due to improper working methods, and strive to minimize the negative impact of case handling.

16. Exploring and improving the coordination mechanism should correctly handle the following relationships: First, the relationship between legality review and coordination. The people's courts should handle administrative disputes through coordination on the premise of clarifying facts, distinguishing right from wrong, and not harming national interests, public interests, or the legitimate rights and interests of others. Second, the relationship between voluntary withdrawal and active coordination. The plaintiff's application for withdrawal must be based on voluntariness; the court must not express the parties' intentions on their behalf, let alone force the parties to accept certain conditions. Third, the relationship between coordination and adjudication. If the parties do not agree to withdraw or later renege on a settlement, the trial should be resumed and a judgment should be rendered in a timely manner, and the court should not pursue a withdrawal rate one-sidedly and fail to render a judgment when it should, dragging on without conclusion. Fourth, the relationship between withdrawal and enforcement. At the same time as confirming the validity of the parties' agreement, if the obligations that should be performed immediately according to the agreement have not been performed, the ruling should not be served hastily; for obligations with an agreed future performance date, supervision should be exercised over the performance of the obligated party to prevent cycle litigation due to breach of contract or bad faith.

17. We must clearly recognize the severe situation of the increasing number of collective administrative disputes, continuously improve the judicial ability to properly handle collective administrative cases according to law, and in accordance with the requirements of the Notice on Properly Handling Collective Administrative Cases issued by the Supreme People's Court, investigate and analyze the situation of collective administrative cases within the jurisdiction, formulate corresponding work plans and measures, and earnestly implement various work measures, fully leveraging the positive role of the people's courts in maintaining social harmony and stability under the unified coordination of the Party committee and with the cooperation and support of the government.

VI. Accurately Apply Legal Norms and Maintain Uniformity of the Legal System

18. The procedure for submitting questions on the application of legal norms must be strictly regulated. When encountering difficult issues in the application of law in trying administrative cases, people's courts at all levels may seek instructions from higher courts. The reporting of instructions should strictly comply with the provisions of the Supreme People's Court on instruction issues, and the content of instructions should be limited to issues concerning the application of laws and judicial interpretations, and should not involve issues of fact-finding, characterization, or substantive handling of the case, nor should the entire case be submitted for instructions. Questions on the application of law should be submitted level by level, not skipping levels. The court requesting instructions shall be responsible for the facts of the issue, and after discussion by the judicial committee, propose a tendency opinion.

19. Correctly handle the issue of overlap between administrative litigation cases and civil litigation cases. The time of occurrence of liability, whether the law has specific provisions on the order of realization of liability, and whether national interests or public interests are involved should be distinguished, and the conflict between civil liability and administrative liability should be resolved prudently. We should base on the national conditions of the primary stage of socialism in China, pay attention to ensuring timely and effective relief for civil victims, and also take into account the basic fairness of bearing both administrative and civil compensatory liabilities. Where the choice of civil or administrative remedies is not clearly defined by law, internal communication and consultation within the court should be strengthened, and the plaintiff's right to administrative or civil litigation should not be easily denied. If the disputed civil legal relationship is the basic and prerequisite fact and the main constituent element for the legality of an administrative act, the administrative litigation should be suspended first, awaiting the judgment of the civil litigation. Conversely, administrative litigation may proceed first. Different trial divisions or courts should actively strengthen communication and coordination, and must not act independently.

20. Fully respect the res judicata effect of final judgments, and prevent making different judgments on the same facts or the same legal issues. Whether it is an administrative case or a civil case, after the judgment becomes legally effective and before it is changed through statutory procedures, it has binding force on the parties, judicial organs, and other subjects; other courts must not make judgments inconsistent with the effective judgment. Even if the effective judgment is indeed erroneous, it must be corrected through statutory procedures according to law, and the existence of the effective judgment must not be ignored.

21. Attach great importance to the issue of "substituting fines for criminal punishment." Currently, in administrative procedures, the phenomenon of "substituting fines for criminal punishment" is relatively prominent. When discovering in administrative adjudication that illegal acts have constituted crimes, people's courts at all levels should promptly transfer the case to criminal investigation organs for handling; where there may be a problem of administrative organs "substituting fines for criminal punishment" or condoning crimes, judicial suggestions should be promptly made to the administrative organs or relevant departments.

VII. Establish a Positive Interaction Mechanism between the Judiciary and the Administration

22. The people's courts should adopt various methods to strengthen communication and exchange with relevant government departments and reconsideration agencies, exchange information on administrative adjudication and administrative law enforcement, and increase mutual understanding and consensus; analyze problems in administrative law enforcement and make judicial suggestions, assist administrative organs in summing up experience and lessons, and improve administrative procedure systems; assist administrative organs in strengthening the education and training of administrative law enforcement personnel, enhancing their awareness of the rule of law and law enforcement level; invite administrative reconsideration and administrative law enforcement personnel to observe the hearings of typical cases, enhancing their concept of law-based administration and ability to respond to lawsuits; publicize and promote experiences and practices that value and support administrative adjudication; report or expose typical cases of illegal interference with administrative adjudication or obstruction of administrative litigation, maintaining litigation order and legal dignity.

23. When communicating and exchanging with relevant government departments and reconsideration agencies, the people's courts should properly handle the relationship between judicial power and administrative power. The people's courts must not participate in the handling of specific administrative cases by administrative organs, nor participate in specific law enforcement activities organized by administrative organs, so as to maintain judicial neutrality and credibility.

24. People's courts shall affirm and support administrative leaders appearing in court to respond to lawsuits. The appearance of local government and administrative department leaders in court demonstrates the importance, support, and respect for administrative adjudication work. It is also a welcome phenomenon reflecting the elevation of the national rule of law level and the progress of social civilization. This plays a significant role and has important significance in enhancing administrative organs' awareness of litigation and their ability to respond to lawsuits, improving the quality and efficiency of trials, properly resolving administrative disputes, and raising the level of law enforcement.

25. People's courts should not impose rigid requirements or mandatory provisions on the appearance of the legal representatives of administrative organs in court to respond to lawsuits. However, they may make recommendations to administrative organs or relevant departments and carry out publicity efforts to promote the healthy development of this work. For the appearance of principal leaders of administrative organs in court to respond to lawsuits, cases that are significant in nature, of widespread public concern, and have normative and educational significance may be selected. People's courts may also make recommendations to administrative organs based on the specific circumstances of the case and the needs of the adjudication work.

VIII. Attaching Importance to and Strengthening Leadership over Administrative Adjudication Work

26. The understanding of the importance of administrative adjudication work shall be further elevated. Leaders of people's courts at all levels must stand from the political and overall perspectives, from the height of strengthening constitutional construction, and from the height of the consistency between law-based administration and democratic governance, to further enhance their understanding of the importance of administrative adjudication work and place the strengthening and improvement thereof in a more prominent position. It is necessary to rectify the erroneous view that administrative adjudication is dispensable or even that it causes trouble, to dare to uphold the authority of the Constitution and laws, to dare to fulfill the supervisory duties entrusted to people's courts by the Constitution and laws, to dare to support and embolden administrative adjudication personnel, and to dare to resolutely resist illegal interference. Through our highly effective work, we shall create a favorable environment where laws are obeyed, governance is supported, governance is smooth, and people are harmonious.

27. Leadership over administrative adjudication work shall be strengthened. It is necessary to comprehensively understand and grasp the status of administrative adjudication work in the court itself and within its jurisdiction, learn from and draw upon the experience of relevant courts in carrying out administrative adjudication work, study and formulate plans, objectives, and measures for carrying out administrative adjudication work, and earnestly implement each measure. It is necessary to promptly understand and earnestly resolve the problems and difficulties that arise in the practice of administrative adjudication. For issues that are difficult for the administrative division and the assigned vice president to resolve in their work, the president shall personally step in to handle the matter. It is necessary to care for and protect administrative adjudication personnel, support them in lawfully performing their duties, and ensure the occupational safety of administrative adjudication judges. The presidents and assigned vice presidents of people's courts at all levels may strive to handle a few administrative cases each year, personally serving as the presiding judge in court hearings to improve their professional capabilities and leadership skills. Based on local realities, quantified assessment standards or requirements for administrative adjudication work shall be formulated, serving as important content of target management and evaluation, and efforts shall be earnestly made to supervise, inspect, implement, and report.

IX. Further Strengthening the Construction of the Administrative Adjudication Team

28. Ideological and political construction and integrity building shall be strengthened. It is necessary to continue to deeply carry out education and practice activities on the socialist rule of law concept, further clarify the guiding ideology of the judiciary, correct judicial concepts, standardize judicial conduct, improve trial style, and ensure judicial integrity. It is necessary to earnestly carry out integrity building and anti-corruption work, seriously investigate and punish a small number of persons who take bribes and pervert the law, engage in graft and malpractice for personal gain, or engage in "power-for-power transactions," and resolutely correct unhealthy practices that harm the interests of the masses. Systems such as accountability for illegal case handling, case quality evaluation, and evaluation, rewards and punishments, and reporting shall be further improved and perfected. At the same time, it is necessary to protect the occupational safety of judges, prevent and stop all acts of retaliation, false accusations, and harm against judges, and lawfully safeguard the personal safety and lawful rights and interests of judges.

29. Increase the training efforts for administrative adjudication personnel and further improve their quality. It is necessary to vigorously strengthen professional training for administrative adjudication personnel. Attention shall be paid both to the study and training of theoretical knowledge of administrative law and to training in trial practice and practical operational skills. Attention shall be paid both to improving knowledge of administrative litigation and trial professional capabilities and to strengthening the study of specialized knowledge in relevant administrative management fields. Efforts shall be earnestly made to enhance the capabilities of administrative adjudication judges in serving the overall situation; in communication and coordination; in presiding over court hearings; in mass work; in drafting adjudicative documents; and in investigation and research. The Supreme People's Court and the High People's Courts shall formulate plans for professional training of administrative adjudication personnel each year, earnestly organize their implementation, and ensure their implementation. For newly promulgated laws and regulations and newly issued judicial interpretations, training shall be organized in a timely manner. It is necessary to earnestly summarize and adhere to successful experiences and effective practices in strengthening court professional construction and improving judges' judicial capabilities, and adopt various forms to enhance the professional quality of administrative adjudication personnel.

30. Improve administrative adjudication institutions, allocate adjudication personnel, and stabilize the adjudication team. It is necessary to further improve administrative adjudication institutions and allocate sufficient administrative adjudication personnel. Except for individual local courts that truly cannot meet the requirements due to an excessively small staffing quota, basic-level courts must ensure the formation of one collegial panel, and intermediate-level courts and above must form two or more collegial panels. This work shall be implemented urgently and completed by the end of this year if possible. The characteristics of administrative adjudication work shall be fully considered, and personnel who are competent and suitable for administrative adjudication work shall be selected and assigned to the administrative division. The issue of the chief judge of the administrative division entering the adjudication committee shall be earnestly addressed. Among the full-time members of the court's adjudication committee, consideration shall also be given to including persons familiar with administrative adjudication work. A group of professional backbones and senior judges with administrative adjudication experience and systematic training shall be retained, and they shall not be easily reassigned or transferred except for promotion to important positions, so as to ensure the relative stability of the administrative adjudication team. Assessment and incentive mechanisms that conform to the characteristics of administrative adjudication work shall be established. The quantity of cases alone shall not be used as a basis for measuring the importance of adjudication work or evaluating the work performance of administrative adjudication judges.
